title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: S is a scheme whose residue characteristics are all different from 2. X is a P^1-bundle over S, i.e. a Brauer–Severi scheme of relative dimension 1, equivalently a conic bundle. G = Aut_S(X) is the corresponding form of PGL(2)_S; Grothendieck's NB notes that giving X/S is equivalent to giving this form. This is the standard correspondence between P^1-bundles and PGL_2-torsors, i.e. inner forms.

The theorem compares three sets.
(a) A(X): subgroup schemes V of G that are étale-locally isomorphic to the constant Klein four-group. Grothendieck writes it as the dihedral group of order 4, (D_4)_S or D_2 on the previous page.
(b) B(X): subgroup schemes Γ of G that are étale-locally isomorphic to the constant symmetric group (S_4)_S.
(c) 'Regular octahedral configurations' in X. These are relative étale divisors Δ of degree 6 in X/S, carrying an 'antipodism' σ_Δ: a fixed-point-free involution on each geometric fibre, so that Δ is cut into three antipodal pairs. The condition is that the group scheme Aut^+_oct(Δ) of orientation-preserving octahedral automorphisms (≅ S_4 locally) acts on X compatibly with its action on Δ. The page writes 'icosaédrales' and 'Aut^+_fact', clearly slips for octahedral.

Claim: there is a transitive system of canonical bijections between (a), (b) and (c). The maps are given on the next page:
- (a→b) Γ = Norm_G(V).
- (b→a) V is the unique normal finite étale subgroup of degree 4 in Γ, with Γ/V ≅ Aut(V) ≅ S_3.
- (c→b) Γ = Aut_S(X,Δ) ≅ Aut^+_oct(Δ).
- (a→c) Each nontrivial section of V gives an involution of X; its two fixed points form an 'axis'. Δ is (étale-locally) the union of the three axes, and the antipodism exchanges the two points of each axis.

Geometrically, over an algebraically closed field this is Klein's octahedral configuration {0, ∞, ±1, ±i} on P^1. Its stabiliser in PGL_2 is S_4, which is the normaliser of the Klein group {z ↦ ±z, ±1/z}. The page states a relative, scheme-theoretic version of this classical picture.

It serves the larger project of the manuscript, moduli of elliptic curves away from characteristic 2. Corollary 2 on the next page turns the theorem into an equivalence between such pairs (X,Δ) and finite étale covers of degree 4 (combinatorial octahedra / S_4-torsor data). This links level-2 structures and the x-line of an elliptic curve to the binary octahedral symmetry.
errors: Item (c) says 'configurations icosaédrales' although the theorem concerns octahedral configurations (degree 6, S_4). The first line of the page already corrects icosa→octa, so this is a slip.
'Aut^+_fact(Δ)' should read Aut^+_oct(Δ), the orientation-preserving octahedral automorphism group scheme.
The klein group is written (D_4)_S here and D_{2S} on the previous page. The notation is inconsistent, but both mean the dihedral group of order 4, i.e. the Klein four-group.

Minor gap: the statement is fine for residue characteristic 3 as well (S_4 ≅ PGL_2(F_3), and the six points stay distinct). This is not commented on, but no correction is needed; the hypothesis char ≠ 2 is exactly right, since Klein subgroups of PGL_2 in char 2 behave differently.
The defining condition of the antipodism ('qui ... fixe sur chaque fibre géom.') is partly crossed out. The intended meaning is 'sans point fixe sur chaque fibre géométrique'.

ideas.what: Bijection between Klein-four subgroup schemes, S_4 subgroup schemes (normaliser) and octahedral 6-point divisors in a P^1-bundle

ideas.modern_name: S_4 ⊂ hyperoctahedral group; orientation cover via the sign character

deep.surprise_reason: This is a clean scheme-theoretic restatement of Klein's octahedral configuration in a P^1-bundle over a base with 2 invertible. It is mathematically correct and fairly routine for a specialist (normaliser of V_4 in PGL_2 is S_4). It is unpublished as phrased, but it contains nothing a specialist would find new.
transcription_corrections: In (c), 'configurations icosaédrales' is in the manuscript, but it is a slip for 'octaédrales'.

'munis de un antipodisme' should read 'munis d'un antipodisme'. The following 'qui ... fixe sur chaque fibre géom.' should be understood as 'sans point fixe sur chaque fibre géom.' (the middle words are struck out).
'GP(1)_S' is Grothendieck's notation for the projective group of P^1, i.e. PGL(2)_S. Also, 'compatible avec son orientation sur Δ' is more plausibly 'avec son opération sur Δ'.
